title: I'm pet sitting an old dog. Every night at two, barking starts in the basement.
transcript:
I'm pet sitting an old dog. Every night at two, barking starts in the basement. The barking started at two, sharp and frantic, somewhere under the floor.

I was pet sitting for my aunt's neighbors. One old golden dog named Biscuit, two pages of instructions, and a note at the bottom. Biscuit is deaf, and he lost his bark years ago, so he won't wake you.

I figured he'd gotten shut in the basement. I went down to the kitchen. His crate was open. Empty.

The barking came from behind the basement door. Then scratching. Then a whine, so close to the gap under the door I felt the air move on my feet.

So I grabbed the handle. "Biscuit, come on, buddy."

The barking stopped. And a man's voice, right on the other side, said, "Good boy. Now let me up."

I let go. I ran upstairs and shut myself in the bedroom, and there was Biscuit, under the bed. Shaking. Silent. Staring past me at the door.

Footsteps climbed the stairs. Slow. Then scratching started on my bedroom door, low down, where a dog would scratch.

Then the barking. Right outside.

Biscuit hasn't barked in years.
